frontier.hypothesis: An ordinary-C form exists that makes expand emit the return value's zero directly into HARD $v0 before block 1's branch, which is what bars $v0 from block 2's local allocation and reproduces the target's whole seat cascade including the sixth callee-save
frontier.mechanism: DECL_RESULT of a scalar-returning function has the hard return register as its RTL, so expand_return writes $v0 directly; local_alloc only respects HARD regs, so only a hard $v0 set (not a function-scope pseudo) can keep block 2's local qtys off $v0

frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c block_alloc / find_free_reg scan hard regs in plain ascending order (MIPS defines no REG_ALLOC_ORDER) and run before global_alloc, so function-scope pseudos are invisible to them
